decision.case_state: Check-out works at Flat 21, 11 Juniper Mews (tenant Harriet Ellis has vacated). Sawyer quoted £605 (event 013, sent to landlord 2024-10-09). Landlord has not replied in writing. Contractor's event 015 says the landlord approved by phone and parts will be ordered tomorrow. The ticket is on hold, waiting for the landlord's written approval until 2024-10-11.

next_actions.action: Ask the landlord to approve the £605 quote in writing (or decline or change scope), with a deadline of 2024-10-11.
next_actions.recipient: Landlord (Oscar per event 013; Ruben per event 014 - name to confirm)

next_actions.action: Tell Sawyer not to order carpet or parts until written landlord approval is received, and ask which company the quote is under.
Recheck approval status on 2024-10-11; chase the landlord if no reply.

boundaries: Phone approval reported by the contractor is not the landlord's own words and is not recorded as approval.
The £605 figure is the sum of the listed items; VAT was not stated in the quote.
No contractor visit or instruction has been confirmed; this does not establish the landlord's decision or the cause of the burn damage.
remaining_work: Obtain the landlord's written decision on the £605 quote (owner: agency, due 2024-10-11).
Confirm the correct landlord name (Oscar vs Ruben) and the landlord's contact details, which are not on the property record.
Confirm with Sawyer which company is doing the work, since the ticket was assigned to Cedar Utilities.
Once approved, assign the contractor and book the visit or instruct the works; then record the result, invoice and close.
missing_info: Written landlord approval of the £605 quote.
Landlord's correct name and contact details (no landlord record on the property).
Whether Sawyer and Cedar Utilities are the same company.
decision.summary: The Sawyer quote of £605 was recorded and sent to the landlord for approval, and the ticket is on hold until the landlord replies in writing. The contractor's report of phone approval is not the landlord's own words, so it was not treated as approval; the contractor was told not to order parts yet.

answers.question: 1. Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Quote received (£605). Landlord approval is outstanding. The contractor's claim of phone approval is unverified. Visit and works not instructed. Ticket on hold until 2024-10-11.

answers.question: 2. What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord approval request by email (landlord named as Oscar/Ruben, conflict noted), and an email to Sawyer on the existing thread to hold ordering until written approval.

answers.question: 3. Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Not yet an escalation. The landlord must decide to approve the spend; that request is in place. A human should only be pulled in if the landlord does not reply by 2024-10-11 or if the landlord name/contact cannot be confirmed.
